audit.why: 55.12% over 2228 games at diff 6/10. Riven owns 2 through first item because every Sion tool is telegraphed — a charged Q, a shield that arms on a timer, an 800-range poke — and none of it stops a 250-range dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven level-chart rows disagree with the packet chart, and four also contradict their own why-text. Packet is [Skill, Riven, Riven, Riven, Riven, Riven, Skill]; both layers hold [Riven, Skill, Sion, Sion, Riven, Sion, Sion].
audit.why: whys[0] says 'Sion has no damage at Level 1' under win[0]=Riven — even, not won. whys[2] calls Level 3 'your clearest ownership window' under win[2]=Sion. whys[3] says 'Your combo speed and sustained auto-weaving keep the edge' under win[3]=Sion. whys[5] says 'your burst now deletes him' under win[5]=Sion. A 55% win rate does not come from a champion who loses four of the seven rows.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 6 -> Skill; rows 1, 2, 3, 5 -> Riven, in both layers, ratings re-pointed, phases[0].why and phases[6].why rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabrications. (a) whys[4] and spikes[1].text both tell you Blade of the Exile 'extends your melee range past his W shield radius' — Soul Furnace is a self-shield, not a radius you can stand outside of; the phrase describes nothing that exists. (b) content.early calls Roar of the Slayer 'his E shield-break poke'. Riot's E text: it damages, slows and REDUCES THE ARMOR of the first enemy hit, at 800 range, and knocks a minion back through everyone behind it. No shield-breaking anywhere.
audit.why: The real Soul Furnace interaction is a timer, and it is the most useful thing on the page: 'Sion shields himself and can reactivate after 3 SECONDS to deal Magic Damage to enemies nearby.' The detonation is on a three-second fuse, so a combo that starts and finishes inside it never eats the payload. And the E is an armour shred that makes your next trade worse, not a shield-break — which also means he can knock a minion into you from 800 range while you are mid-Q-chain.
audit.corrected: whys[4], spikes[1].text, wants.foe[1] and content.early rewritten onto the 3-second arming window and the real armour-shred E.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both flagged missing interactions are absent from the content layer. The page never states that Glory in Death heals him, nor that his damage is max-health based and therefore ignores the armour the itemization line tells you to buy.
audit.why: Glory in Death: 'His attacks become very rapid, heal him, and deal bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health.' The anti-heal TIMING is the whole point — Grievous Wounds must already be applied when he dies, because the zombie is what does the healing. Buying it after he reanimates is too late. Soul Furnace is also flagged percentHealth, so stacking raw HP against him is self-defeating.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal timing written into content.late and spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page names Decimating Smash as the tracked cooldown but never gives a number, and never gives Soul Furnace's either.
audit.why: Q is 10/9/8/7/6s and W is 15/14/13/12/11s — the W is the longer and more punishable of the two, yet the page builds its whole tracking loop around the Q.
audit.corrected: Soul Furnace's 3-second arming delay added where it is actionable; left the Q framing alone since it is not wrong, only secondary.

edits.before: Your Q resets win level 1 if you weave autos between casts. Identify how Sion contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Level 1 is even: Sion has no damage without a charged Decimating Smash and you have no W. Farm at Q tip and stay clear of bush corners.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Sion carry threat 7/10 â€” close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on: armour and health blunt your burst and Glory in Death buys him a second life. Win through objectives, not a clean solo kill.

edits.before: Blade of the Exile extends your reach past his W shield radius and Wind Slash executes him out of zombie state — your most decisive kill window all lane.
edits.after: Blade of the Exile plus Wind Slash beat Soul Furnace — the shield only detonates 3 seconds after he casts it, so burst inside that fuse and his answer never fires.

edits.before: Blade of the Exile extends your melee range past his W shield radius and Wind Slash executes him the moment his W shield pops or he zombies out.
edits.after: Blade of the Exile plus Wind Slash beats his Soul Furnace window — but land Grievous Wounds before he dies, because his zombie autos heal off your max HP.

edits.before: At Level 1 Sion wants to walk up and threaten a charged Q knockup — stay at Q-tip range, last-hit, and do not let him funnel you into a bush corner where he can channel unseen. The moment W unlocks at Level 2 you have a genuine all-in: dash onto him with Q1, W-stun to cancel any charging Q, then Q2-Q3-E-auto weave to cash your passive. His W shield is not up yet at Level 2 if you engage immediately, so this is your cleanest window. At Level 3 the pattern is the same but richer: use E defensively to eat his E shield-break poke, then re-engage when his W is down — a full Q chain with passive autos between every cast melts him before he can respond.
edits.after: At Level 1 Sion wants to walk up and threaten a charged Q knockup — stay at Q-tip range, last-hit, and do not let him funnel you into a bush corner where he can channel unseen. The moment W unlocks at Level 2 you have a genuine all-in: dash onto him with Q1, W-stun to cancel any charging Q, then Q2-Q3-E-auto weave to cash your passive. His W shield is not up yet at Level 2 if you engage immediately, so this is your cleanest window. At Level 3 the pattern is richer: hold E for Roar of the Slayer, which shreds your armour from 800 range and can knock a minion back through you, then re-engage — a full Q chain with passive autos between every cast melts him before he answers.

edits.before: Pop W shield pre-emptively to absorb your burst window and force you to disengage
edits.after: Pre-cast Soul Furnace so its 3-second detonation lands exactly as your combo commits

edits.before: A two-item Sion with Sunfire and Heartsteel will absorb your burst and zombie-walk back through your wave even if you win the fight — stop trying to 1v1 kill him in a side-wave and instead use your split-push pressure to force a response while your team takes objectives. In teamfights Wind Slash is your tool: let Sion engage with Unstoppable Onslaught, clean up the chaos in his wake, and execute whoever his ult displaced into low HP. Do not hard-commit your full combo into a full-tank Sion with three armor items unless his W shield is already down.
edits.after: A two-item Sion with Sunfire and Heartsteel absorbs your burst and zombie-walks back through your wave even when you win the fight — and Glory in Death heals him off your MAXIMUM health, so Grievous Wounds has to be on him before he dies, never after. Stop trying to 1v1 him in a side-wave; split-push to force a response while your team takes objectives. In teamfights Wind Slash is your tool: let Sion engage with Unstoppable Onslaught, clean up behind the charge, and execute whoever it displaced. Never commit the full combo while his Soul Furnace is still armed.

notes: content.early and wants.you[0] both claim your W stun cancels a charging Decimating Smash. Riot's Q text does not describe the charge as an interruptible channel and the kit carries no channel flag on it, so I could not verify the claim from the kits — I left both strings untouched rather than delete advice that may well be correct. Recorded in unverified; it deserves a wiki check because the entire Level 2 gameplan on this page rests on it.
